messages:
ania: quick Q about prefix cache semantics for the new prompt-level caching work — trying to nail down what we surface to clients (headers/body) and how invalidation should propagate
leo: do you mean for the API response when a request is served from prefix cache vs full-response cache?
sasha: also: key composition — do we tie keys to model sha, hyperparams, or only prefix content?
ania: yes to both. Wanted to propose a concrete contract and get :eyes: before I open the PR. Proposal below.
leo: paste it, please.
ania: Proposal (summary):
- Response headers: X-Redwood-Cache: HIT|MISS; key=<short-key>
- Response body meta: "cache_hit": true|false (optional; only for JSON responses)
- Cache-Control: set to "private, max-age=0, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=30" for hosted API when we allow shared infra to revalidate
- Cache key format: "prefixcache:v3::{model}:{model_sha}:{prefix_hash}:{prompt_schema_hash}:{client_tier}"
- Invalidation: publish invalidation messages on "prefix-cache-invalidate" topic with either exact key or prefix (support wildcard tombstones).
- Backcompat: v2 keys remain readable; new writes use v3 namespace so old clients get conservative behavior.

sasha: couple questions: why both header and body? duplication seems odd.
ania: header for infra + proxies + observability (fast), body flag to make it easy for app-level metrics without parsing headers. Many clients log response bodies but not headers. Also some SDKs make body metadata available on the high-level response object.
leo: sounds reasonable. We should keep body flag optional to avoid bloating small responses like embeddings. Maybe only include body flag for streaming/chat/generation endpoints, not embeddings.
ania: agreed. I'll limit body meta to generation endpoints. I'll add opt-out via request param ?cache_meta=false for advanced clients.

morgan: about key composition: do we need temperature/seed? If temperature changes, outputs differ but prefix cache only applies to deterministic prefix continuation.
sasha: good point. I think key should NOT include temperature if we only cache prefix tokens used to prime the KV cache; but if we cache *generated* tokens for a particular temperature, that's invalid. We should document: prefix cache keys only cover deterministic prefix-to-KV mapping. If client requests sampling-based generation, we still can use prefix cache (to fill kv cache) but not serve cached generated tail.
leo: say that in contract: prefix cache semantics = "only reuse cached KV/prefix state; model must be re-run for generation steps". If client passes deterministic flags (top_p=1, temp=0, do_sample=false) then we can optionally serve full cached response if present.
ania: added: full-response cache is separate namespace. Good.

deploy-bot: deploy "prefix-cache-service@staging" succeeded in 10m (logs: ok)
ania: timing note: invalidation propagation SLA target = <1s to all nodes in region> via pubsub; if a node misses it, tombstones last 5m and revalidate on first hit.
morgan: propagation via Kafka? We should avoid cross-region sync for now; do regional topics and a cross-region bridge if needed later.
leo: agree regional-first. Add sequence numbers to invalidation messages so we can reconcile missed messages on reconnect.
sasha: what about key leakage — X-Redwood-Cache contains key=... could that expose sensitive prompt prefixes? We should only expose a truncated hash (8-12 chars) and never raw prefix text.
ania: yes, header will have short key hash only. No plaintext prefixes. Also ensure we don't log full prefixes in access logs.

ania: roll out plan:
- canary on 5% of traffic (eng-sre traffic tag) with header+body flag enabled for generation endpoints
- after 1 week of metrics (hit ratio, false-hit checks), expand to 50%
- full rollout after 2 weeks and docs update

morgan: tests required in PR: unit tests for key generation (including model sha changes), integration test asserting X-Redwood-Cache header on hit, simulate invalidation event and ensure subsequent request is MISS then re-populates cache, security test ensuring header key length <= 12 and not containing plaintext.
sasha: also add e2e that checks that when model version increments we use v3 namespace and don't erroneously serve old model responses.
leo: one more: telemetry — include cache metrics in per-route dashboards (hits, misses, stale-served, invalidations/sec). We should add SLOs for stale-serving rate <0.1%.

ania: small open Q for reviewers: should invalidation accept full key lists only, or allow wildcard prefixes like "model:abc:*"? Wildcards are powerful but could be abused.
sasha: prefer explicit keys + a separate "namespace invalidation" API for model-level flushes (internal only). No wildcard in public invalidation.
leo: agree. namespace invalidation will be authenticated and only allowed by admin roles.

ania: tagging reviewers: @leo @sasha @morgan — PTAL when you can, I'll start the PR with code + tests tomorrow.
leo: happy to review. Ping me in CR and mark w/ "cache-contract" label.
sasha: I'll add unit tests stubs.
morgan: I'll add the telemetry dashboards.
ania: thanks all :thumbsup:
leo: small nit: change header name to X-Redwood-Cache-Status? less ambiguous.
ania: ok X-Redwood-Cache-Status: HIT|MISS; key=abcd1234

morgan: Ack, will update the checklist and CR description. I'll also put a note in eng-oncall channel about the invalidate topic.
ania: awesome — I'll draft PR now.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout to canary group at 2026-03-18T16:00:00Z
ania: noted. last question: should older clients (pre-contract) get any change?
leo: no breaking changes — header is additive, body meta opt-in. If a client expects no header, nothing breaks. Document it in the API compatibility notes.
ania: perfect. I'll include migration docs and sample snippets for SDKs.
sasha: nice. done for now.
ania: thanks everyone!
